content.text:
The document fully satisfies the preferred position. My verification:

- **Customer convenience right (§ 9.4)**: Customer may terminate the Agreement *or any Order Form* without cause; Customer owes only accrued Fees and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period — a pro-rata refund with no early-termination fee or penalty.
- **Notice period (§ 29.4)**: The cross-reference resolves to "thirty days before the effective termination date" — exactly the preferred 30 days.
- **No Vendor convenience right**: A full sweep of "terminate" shows Vendor's only termination rights are for material breach (§ 9.1) and insolvency (§ 9.2), both mutual and for-cause. Vendor has no without-cause right during the three-year term (§ 8.1), and § 20.5 and § 24.4 further restrict Vendor from terminating unaffected Services or terminating on Customer's change of control.
- **No early-termination charges**: § 10 imposes refund obligations on Vendor, not exit fees on us. (§ 7.7's punitive late-payment liquidated damages is a payment-terms issue outside this rule's scope.)

input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
input.rationale: Meets the preferred position in full. Section 9.4 gives Customer a without-cause termination right over the Agreement and any Order Form, with the notice period resolving via Section 29.4 to thirty days before the effective termination date. Customer owes only accrued Fees and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, so there is a pro-rata refund and no early-termination fee or penalty. Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right: its only termination rights are mutual for-cause rights for material breach (9.1) and insolvency (9.2), and no Vendor convenience right exists during the three-year term under Section 8.1 (confirmed by a full-document sweep for termination rights; Sections 20.5 and 24.4 further bar Vendor from terminating unaffected Services or terminating on Customer change of control). Section 10 imposes refund duties on Vendor rather than exit charges on Customer. No redline required.
